decisions.choice: make his face shine: look on someone with goodwill
decisions.reason: A shining face is a look of favor and delight, the opposite of a face turned away in anger. Psalms ask the same of God (Psalm 31:17; 67:2; 80:4, 8, 20).

decisions.choice: be gracious: show favor freely
decisions.reason: The verb means to show kindness that is not earned, as to someone in need. The LORD uses it of himself in Exodus 33:19.

decisions.choice: look on you with pleasure
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of a shining face instead of keeping it.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun span: "그분의" with the honorific at Literal, and no pronoun at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting the English marks on "his" has nothing to change; respect for God is carried by "그분" and the honorific "-시-", as the Korean style guide sets for the whole Bible. Recorded once for Numbers 6-11.

decisions.choice: faça a sua face brilhar sobre ti (L, B); olhe para ti com alegria (R); seja bondoso contigo (L, R), te mostre o seu favor (B)
decisions.reason: The shining face is a look of goodwill (m1), kept at Literal and Balanced and explained at Readable as the English does. The second verb is kindness freely given (m2): "ser bondoso" and "mostrar o seu favor" say that without the sense of pity in "misericórdia".

decisions.choice: "ፊቱን ወደ አንተ ያብራ" (L), "ፊቱ በአንተ ላይ ያብራ" (B), "በደስታ ይመልከትህ" (R) for "make his face shine toward you"; "ይራራልህ" (L), "ሞገሱን ያድልህ" (B), "ቸርነቱን ያሳይህ" (R) for "be gracious to you"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "toward you" and the single verb; Balanced says "show you favor" with "ሞገስ" (favour, grace freely given, m2); Readable explains the shining face as a look of goodwill (m1), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span ("अपना", "अपने")
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the English deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change in Hindi, and the Hindi text has no deity_pronoun spans. Hindi says "his face" with the reflexive "अपना", and respect for God comes from the honorific plural verbs. The same in verses 26-27.

decisions.choice: "मुख ... चमकाएँ" (L), "मुख का तेज ... डालें" (B), "प्रसन्न होकर ... देखें" (R); "अनुग्रह करना" (L, B), "दया करना" (R)
decisions.reason: A shining face means looking on someone with goodwill (m1). Literal keeps the Hebrew picture, Balanced keeps it in a natural Hindi phrase, and Readable says what it means, as the English does. "Be gracious" is showing favor freely (m2): "अनुग्रह", the word for grace, at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "दया".

decisions.choice: "своё лицо" with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The English has a deity_pronoun span on "his face". Russian uses the reflexive "своё" here, which takes no span, as in the New Testament; the same holds in verse 26.

decisions.choice: "その顔" (L), "顔" (B) with no deity_pronoun span and no honorific prefix
decisions.reason: Japanese has no deity_pronoun spans (style guide 7); the respect is carried by the verb くださる, so the noun stays plain.

decisions.choice: reflexive "своєму лицю" with no deity pronoun span
decisions.reason: Ukrainian refers back to the subject with the reflexive "свій", which the deity pronoun setting leaves alone, so the line has no span where the English has one on "his".

decisions.choice: lift up his face toward you: turn to you with attention and favor
decisions.reason: To lift up the face toward someone is to look at them and pay them heed. The opposite is for God to hide his face, leaving his people alone in trouble (Deuteronomy 31:17-18).

decisions.choice: peace: whole well-being
decisions.reason: The word means wholeness and well-being: safety, health, plenty, and right relations with God and others, not only the absence of war.

decisions.choice: set: give and establish
decisions.reason: The verb is the ordinary word for put or place, the same verb as "put my name" in verse 27. The LORD is asked to make peace the settled state of his people.

decisions.choice: set peace for you
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb "set" so that it matches "set my name" in verse 27. Balanced says "grant" and Readable "give".

decisions.choice: turn toward you and care for you
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the lifted face.

decisions.choice: "qu'il pose sur toi la paix", matching "ils poseront mon nom" in verse 27
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for putting the LORD's name on the people in verse 27 (m3). Literal uses "poser" in both verses to keep the link; Balanced says "accorder" and Readable "donner", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "akuwekee amani", matching "wataliweka jina langu" in verse 27
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for putting the LORD's name on the people in verse 27 (m3). Literal uses "kuweka" in both verses; Balanced says "kujalia" (grant) and Readable "kupa" (give).

decisions.choice: "평안" for shalom
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as whole well-being, not only the absence of war; "평안" says that, and is the word the Korean Psalms use for the LORD's blessing of peace on his people (Psalm 29:11). "평강" is the older church word.

decisions.choice: ponha a paz para ti
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the ordinary verb "pôr" so that it matches "porão o meu nome" in verse 27, as the English keeps "set" (r-en-1). Balanced says "conceder" and Readable "dar". "A paz" is whole well-being (m2).

decisions.choice: "ያኑርልህ" (may he set, establish for you) at Literal; "ይስጥህ" (give) at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is "set, put", that is, give and establish (m3); Literal keeps "put in place". "ሰላም" is the key term for peace, whole well-being (m2).

decisions.choice: "शान्ति रखें"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb "set" as "रखना", so that it matches "they shall set my name" ("मेरा नाम रखेंगे") in verse 27, as the English Literal does. Peace is whole well-being (m2), "शान्ति" at every level.

decisions.choice: "установит тебе мир" (L); "подарит" (B); "даст" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew verb "set" (sim), as the English Literal does, so that it matches "they shall set my name" in verse 27. Peace here is whole well-being (m2).

decisions.choice: shalom "平安"
decisions.reason: Whole well-being given to a person, which the NT table renders 平安 (inner peace, blessing), not 平和 between parties.

decisions.choice: put my name on them: mark them as belonging to the LORD
decisions.reason: Speaking the LORD's name over the people three times claims them as his. To be called by the LORD's name is to belong to him (Deuteronomy 28:10; 2 Chronicles 7:14).

decisions.choice: and I will bless them: the blessing comes from God himself
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is written out, which Hebrew does for emphasis. The priests speak the words, but it is the LORD who gives the blessing.

decisions.choice: I myself
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced add "myself" to show the emphatic "I"; Readable says "I will be the one".

decisions.choice: eu [mesmo] (L), eu mesmo (B), with no deity_pronoun span
alternatives: eu Mesmo, capitalised under the setting
decisions.reason: The English puts "myself" under the deity_pronoun setting. Portuguese "mesmo" is not a pronoun but a word that agrees with "eu", which never takes a span (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 7), and a capitalised "Mesmo" would read as a mistake; so only "meu" has a span here.

decisions.choice: "ያኖራሉ" (they shall put) for "set my name on", the same verb as "ያኑርልህ" in 6:26 L
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses one verb for setting peace and setting the name (m1); Amharic "አኖረ" keeps the echo at Literal.

decisions.choice: 'put my name on' "わたしの名で呼ぶ" (R)
decisions.reason: R says what the idiom means, that the people are marked as the LORD's own; L and B keep 名を置く.
